svg.text: ORIGINAL RESEARCH
Comparative Effectiveness of Once-Weekly Semaglutide Versus
Sulfonylureas, DPP4 Inhibitors, and Thiazolidinediones in Patients
with Type 2 Diabetes and Chronic Kidney Disease
James Almanao · Jian Wang · Hongdao Liu · Anamoul Sundar · Yan Song · Lin Xie ·
Sherif Mehanam · Josh Noone · Caroline Swift · Matthew R. Weir
Received: April 10, 2024 / Accepted: July 31, 2024 / Published online: August 20, 2024
© The Author(s) 2024. Open Access article under CC BY-NC 4.0 license
ABSTRACT

text.tspan: Once-weekly (OW) semaglutide has shown robust renal and cardiovascular

svg.text: benefits in clinical trials for patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and chronic kidney
disease (CKD). This real-world comparative effectiveness study assessed clinical
outcomes between OW semaglutide and alternative oral glucose-lowering drugs.

text.tspan: Adults with T2D and CKD stages 1–4 were identified from the Optum®

svg.text: de-identified Clinformatics Data Mart Database (2016–2023). Two distinct cohorts
were analyzed: patients receiving OW semaglutide versus DPP4 inhibitors (DPP4i),
sulfonylureas (SU), or thiazolidinediones (TZD). Multivariable Cox proportional
hazards and propensity-score matching balanced baseline clinical covariates.

text.tspan: A total of 14,892 matched patient pairs were evaluated. OW semaglutide

svg.text: was associated with a significantly reduced rate of estimated glomerular filtration
rate (eGFR) decline compared with active comparators (-1.24 vs. -2.85 mL/min/
1.73m²/year; p < 0.001). Risk of progression to end-stage renal disease (ESRD)
or 50% eGFR sustained decline was reduced by 34% (HR 0.66; 95% CI 0.58–0.75).
Significant reductions were also observed in all-cause hospitalizations, composite
cardiovascular endpoints (MACE-3), and mean HbA1c (-0.82% reduction).

text.tspan: In routine clinical practice, once-weekly semaglutide conferred superior

svg.text: kidney and metabolic protective benefits compared to traditional oral regimens.
Keywords: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist · Semaglutide · Chronic kidney disease · Type 2 diabetes · eGFR
